dataset.description: This describes the generated artificial crystal structure data for solving the phase problem using deep learning. It is part of the grant "Solving the Phase Problem in Crystallography with Deep Learning" (No. lzp-2024/1-0220), financed by the Latvian Council of Science. This description ensures data accessibility, reproducibility, and long-term usability. It includes details about its origin, format, structure, and processing methods, allowing researchers to understand, validate, and reuse the data effectively. It enhances data interoperability across different platforms and research communities, ensuring consistency in analysis and facilitating collaboration. Additionally, it helps with compliance to funding agency requirements, improves data preservation, and supports future integration with new datasets or analytical methods, ultimately maximizing the impact and longevity of the research.

distribution.title: Artificial crystal structure data is used to train neural networks to solve the phase problem in crystallography.

dataset.title: Crystallography Phase Problem Generated Data

dmp.description: The project develops and trains several neural networks to solve the phase problem in small molecule crystallography. This will enable methods for determining the structures of large unit cells and solving structures from low-resolution and low-completeness data, where current methods fail to provide solutions. To achieve the goals, efficient and rapid artificial crystal structure generation procedures (in real-time) and procedures for generating diffraction data with varying resolution and completeness, reflecting experimental conditions (e.g., high-pressure experiments or electron diffraction) in reciprocal space are developed for supervised machine learning. The purpose of DMP is to provide a management plan for the generated data.
